messages.content: What parameters do the viscous friction force depend on, and in which case should it be taken into account for the physical pendulum model? In your response the last word of each sentence must become the first word of the next sentence.

message.content: The viscous friction force depends on the velocity of the body and on the damping properties of the surrounding medium. Medium characteristics such as fluid viscosity and density directly set the value of the damping coefficient. Coefficient of damping is what multiplies the angular velocity in the pendulum equation of motion. Motion of a physical pendulum should include this term only when it oscillates in a fluid rather than in a vacuum. Vacuum is the idealized condition under which the viscous force vanishes entirely. Entirely frictionless systems are merely theoretical approximations for real pendulums exposed to air resistance. Resistance from the surrounding air is the dominant viscous effect that must be modeled for accurate predictions of damped oscillation.
